english.title: Contravene direction given to wear face covering within, or leave, a relevant place in England
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, contravened a direction to

(A)_[wear a face covering when entering or in]_
(B)_[leave]_

**(..SPECIFY PLACE..), a relevant place, the direction being given by **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a relevant person who considered that you were not wearing a face covering, in contravention of a requirement to do so under regulation 3 of the Health Protection (Coronavirus, Wearing of Face Coverings in a Relevant Place) (England) Regulations 2020
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 5(2) and 6(3) and (4) of the Health Protection (Coronavirus, Wearing of Face Coverings in a Relevant Place) (England) Regulations 2020.

english.notes:
(i) Please note - whilst this is a summary offence, the offence is not governed by the 6 month time limit that would usually apply to offences as set out in section 127(1) of the Magistrates Court Act 1980. This is because the offence is created by regulations made under the Public Health (Control of Disease) Act 1984. Section 64A of the Public Health (Control of Disease) Act 1984 provides the time limits for this offence, being before the end of the period of 6 months beginning with the date on which evidence which the prosecutor thinks is sufficient to justify the proceedings comes to the prosecutor's knowledge; and within 3 years of the date of the commission of the offence.
(ii) The offence under regulation 6(3), relates to contravening a direction given under regulation 5(2) or regulation 5(5), beingRegulation 5(2) Where a relevant person considers that a person is not wearing a face covering, in contravention of the requirement in regulation 3, the relevant person may -(a) direct that person to wear such a covering;
(b) direct that person to leave the relevant place.Regulation 5(5) Where a relevant person has reasonable grounds to believe that a relevant child is failing to comply with the requirement in regulation 3, the relevant person may direct any individual who has responsibility for the relevant child to secure, so far as reasonably practicable, that the child complies with the requirement.(iii) Regulation 5(9) provides details of who are 'relevant persons' for the purpose of enforcement under regulation 5.
(iv) See regulation 3(2) for details of where the requirement to wear a face covering whilst entering / remaining within a relevant place, do not apply.
(v) See regulation 4(1) for circumstances where an individual will have a reasonable excuse not to wear a face covering.
(vi) The Fixed Penalty Notice (FPN) for this offence is £100, but is £50 if paid before the end of the period of 14 days following the date of the notice. See regulation 7(6) and 7(7) for details.
(vii) Furthermore, regulation 7(7A) (from 28/8/20) provides that a second fixed penalty notice issued is £200; in the case of the third and subsequent fixed penalty notices received, double the amount specified in the last fixed penalty notice received by that person, to a maximum of £3200.
(viii) Fixed Penalty Notice (FPN) for this offence is now £200 with maximum now £6400 as from 24th September, 2020. Therefore new offence under H21740 applies.
